title: How do I find credible sources for a research topic?
problem_statement: You need trustworthy academic sources for an essay, project or report and don't know where to start beyond a general web search.
expected_outcome: A short list of relevant, credible sources saved with their details so you can cite them.

steps.title: Turn your topic into a question
steps.instructions: Write one sentence describing what you want to find out, then list 3–5 key terms and any synonyms.
steps.expected_result: A research question and a list of search terms.

steps.title: Search scholarly literature
steps.instructions: Search Google Scholar with two or three key terms. Use 'Since Year' to focus on recent work and put exact phrases in quotation marks.
steps.expected_result: A first set of results that match your question.

steps.title: Screen using abstracts
steps.instructions: Read titles and abstracts. Keep sources that answer your question; note where each was published.

steps.title: Follow the trail
steps.instructions: Open 'Cited by' and 'Related articles' on your best source to find newer and connected work.
steps.expected_result: A few more relevant sources you would not have found by keywords alone.

steps.title: Save and record
steps.instructions: Save each source to a reference manager so its details are stored for citing later.
steps.expected_result: All selected sources saved with author, title, year and link.

quality_checks: Every source is relevant to your question.
You know where and when each source was published.
Each saved reference opens the original source.

editorial.author: V2 research pass (AI-assisted, Claude)
editorial.change_summary: Researched from official sources 2026-10-21; published under owner's blanket MVP approval (D-044). Domain-expert review pending.

budget_note: Searching is possible without paying; some full texts need a subscription or library access.
alternative_methods: Ask a librarian at your school or public library for subject databases you can access.
common_mistakes: Citing an abstract without reading the paper
Treating every search result as credible
